result.title: Choosing Supervised Post-Processing for Frozen Person Detectors: Information, Object Changes, and Complete Cost
result.summary: A frozen detector computes hypotheses that can support better final outputs through supervised post-processing. Choosing a readout requires knowing which available information improves detection and what its processing costs. We compare candidate scores, class distributions, geometry, native-set summaries and adapted neighborhood meta classification under common candidate, supervision and operating-point conditions. On 320 held-out CrowdHuman images, adding native-set context to a 97-dimensional readout yields 275 more matches and 96 more unmatched predictions. On a separate 319-image cohort, Full100 matches 6004 objects,versus 5848 for source-selected raw WBF and 6002 for a MetaDetect-style adaptation. Its gain over raw contains 300 added and 144 lost discoveries. After execution-equivalent optimization, Full100 and the meta-statistics readout both take approximately 95 ms per complete warm request on a fixed 64-image workload. Source-frozen transfer gives positive point results on 223 MOT17Det frames from seven sequences, while the main MIAP result shows no improvement. The study supports using sufficiently informative output readouts while retaining optimized meta classification as a competitive option. It also shows why feature dimension and net detection gain alone are unreliable guides to adoption.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在冻结行人检测器上比较候选分数、类别分布、几何、原生集合摘要与邻域元分类等多种监督式后处理读出，在 CrowdHuman、MOT17Det 等数据上报告匹配增益与完整请求延迟，并指出特征维度与净检测增益都不足以指导采用决策。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「冻结表示＋替换读出所含信息＋完整成本核算」的评估框架，可能为 LVR 中核查答案是否真正使用视觉细节、以及权衡计算开销与收益（如 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的成本端）提供概念参照，但属检测后处理，迁移线索需较多核查。
